project.boundarySource: Historic Environment Scotland CRAIL Conservation Area, buffered 300m for settlement study
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 2 of 14. Strict settlement merit, See, café-led Eat, all named trail providers, picnic, public visitor parking, public toilets, access, transport, dogs and complete local HES/NRHE construction dates were checked before continuing. The Shoregate, Golf Hotel, Balcomie Links Hotel and fish-bar meal offer were removed from Eat under the café-led brief. Balcomie Links and Fife Ness remain separate localities.

touristAppeal.label: Strong Destination
touristAppeal.summary: Crail remains a strong East Neuk destination for its harbour, historic streets, museum, pottery, church, coastal walking and live treasure trail. Its Eat list now contains only verified café, coffee, cake and light-lunch stops.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Very good for harbour, shore, coastal walking and the dog-welcoming gallery, but not fully dog-equivalent: pet-dog admission is unconfirmed at the museum, pottery access is only partly evidenced, and several eating places restrict dogs to particular areas.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Harbour and Shoregate
visitorHighlights.reason: The defining East Neuk harbour scene, reached through the old burgh lanes.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Welcome to Fife / Fife Council visitor evidence

editorialReview.scoreRationale: The defining East Neuk harbour scene, reached through the old burgh lanes.

visitorHighlights.name: Roome Bay and Rock Pools
visitorHighlights.reason: A south-facing sandy cove with extensive rock pools, a wildlife-rich former bathing pool, play space, public toilets and direct access to the Fife Coastal Path.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air beach and greenspace; visit in daylight and check tides and current water-quality advice.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A south-facing sandy cove with extensive rock pools, a wildlife-rich former bathing pool, play space, public toilets and direct access to the Fife Coastal Path.

attractionGuide.headline: Rock pools, wildlife and coastal air
attractionGuide.intro: A compact south-facing bay for low-tide exploring, family time and a gentle coast-path stop.
attractionGuide.parking: Free parking facilities are listed by Fife Council; spaces, bay layout and maximum stay are not published for this beach facility.
attractionGuide.toilets: Public toilets are listed by Fife Council at Roome Bay.
attractionGuide.picnic: No dedicated picnic tables are confirmed; the sloping grass and benches provide informal outdoor stopping places.
attractionGuide.foodNote: No on-site café is confirmed; use Crail’s separately researched Eat choices.

trails.name: Fife Coastal Path at Roome Bay
trails.summary: The waymarked coast path crosses the greenspace above the bay.
trails.distance: Choose a short Crail section or continue towards Anstruther or Fife Ness.
trails.difficulty: Steps and sloping paths around the beach.

thingsToDo.name: Explore the rock pools
thingsToDo.summary: Visit around low tide and avoid disturbing wildlife.

thingsToDo.name: See the former bathing pool
thingsToDo.summary: The disused pool at the west end is now a wildlife haven.

thingsToDo.name: Use the play space
thingsToDo.summary: A children’s play area sits above the beach.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Parish Church and Kirkyard
visitorHighlights.reason: A medieval church ensemble with a Pictish cross slab, a nationally notable group of mural monuments and the unusual 1826 Dead House in its historic kirkyard.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Kirkyard open during normal daylight access; church interior is available at services, published openings or by local arrangement.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free; donations welcome when the church is open.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Crail Parish Church and Crail Museum

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A medieval church ensemble with a Pictish cross slab, a nationally notable group of mural monuments and the unusual 1826 Dead House in its historic kirkyard.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Harbour Gallery
visitorHighlights.reason: A restored 17th-century fisherman’s cottage combining a working gallery of locally influenced art with one of Crail’s best sea-view interiors and courtyards.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open daily; operator advises checking the short January closure.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free gallery visit; food and purchases extra.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A genuine working local gallery in a distinctive historic harbour building, with dependable operator visitor information.

visitorHighlights.name: Castle Walk and Viewpoint
visitorHighlights.reason: A short signed walk around the former castle site, with surviving walls, a fossil-mounted sundial, a panoramic indicator and steps towards the harbour.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air public walk; daylight visit recommended.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A short signed walk around the former castle site, with surviving walls, a fossil-mounted sundial, a panoramic indicator and steps towards the harbour.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Priory Doocot
visitorHighlights.reason: A restored beehive doocot with a reconstructed potence ladder, lighting, interpretation and around 700 nest boxes beside Roome Bay.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Exterior and surrounding coastal greenspace open in daylight; interior access is subject to the door being open.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A restored beehive doocot with a reconstructed potence ladder, lighting, interpretation and around 700 nest boxes beside Roome Bay.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Museum and Heritage Centre
visitorHighlights.reason: A focused introduction to the royal burgh, fishing and local life.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Summer 2026: Thursday-Sunday 11:00-16:00 until 18 October, plus the published holiday Monday.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A focused introduction to the royal burgh, fishing and local life.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Pottery
visitorHighlights.reason: A long-established working pottery that adds an independent craft stop.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Welcome to Fife / Fife Council visitor evidence

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A long-established working pottery that adds an independent craft stop.

visitorHighlights.name: Crail Tolbooth and Marketgate
visitorHighlights.reason: Crail’s 1598 civic landmark anchors Marketgate with an early burgh coat of arms, a 1520 bell, clock tower, mercat cross and memorial fountain.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Exterior and Marketgate open at all times; Town Hall interior is event-dependent.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Crail’s 1598 civic landmark anchors Marketgate with an early burgh coat of arms, a 1520 bell, clock tower, mercat cross and memorial fountain.

townGuide.headline: A remarkably complete East Neuk harbour town
townGuide.intro: Crail remains a strong East Neuk destination for its harbour, historic streets, museum, pottery, church, coastal walking and live treasure trail. Its Eat list now contains only verified café, coffee, cake and light-lunch stops.
perfectFor: Visitors who prefer compact, walkable settlements

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Start with Crail Harbour and Shoregate
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Begin at Crail Harbour and Shoregate, then continue through the historic core and along the coast.

townGuide.visitorMood: A strong small destination: the historic burgh and harbour are independently worthwhile, with museum, craft and coastal-path depth inside the settlement.

features.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
features.fullDescription: Originally Romanesque c.1160, remains of chancel (N wall and SW fragment) of that date. West tower c.1200, evidently originally free-standing but designed as part of plan for rebuilt nave: rebuilding of nave implemented c.1120, 6-bay aisled with clerestory, circular piers, new chancel arch pierced at same date. Belfry stage, corbelled parapet and squat stone spire added to tower c.1500 +. North side wall rebuilt 18th century. Nave reconstructed Robert Balfour 1815, new S. aisle wall with splayed gothic windows and wooden tracery. N. wall rewindowed in same manner, continuous roof over nave and aisles; choir shortened, much rebuilt and fitted up with gallery Wm Lees of Pittenweem 1828. Ashlar-built, slated roofs. Balfour and Lees furnishings recently removed and interior recast.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland NRHE / trove.scot Points GIS
sources.coverage: NRHE records whose representative points lie within the authoritative Crail parish extent
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact parish containment
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: The spatial index provides a representative site point, names and classifications. It does not establish construction dates; detailed source records require individual review.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland Scheduled Monuments spatial data
sources.coverage: Scheduled monuments intersecting the strict editorial boundary
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact boundary intersection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: The spatial layer supplies designation and location, not a historic construction period. Undated records remain in the catalogue but are hidden from the heat map.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland Listed Buildings spatial data
sources.coverage: Crail editorial district plus 500m heritage buffer; buffer records are retained as related context
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact polygon selection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: Crail has no separate NRS locality boundary. The transparent visitor-guide editorial boundary is used and buffer records remain context only. The source supplies statutory designation and location metadata, not construction dates.

sources.name: Crail attraction visitor-value assessment
sources.organisation: Crail Museum, Fife Council, Crail Parish Church and attraction operators
sources.coverage: All 44 user-supplied Crail attraction candidates; publication threshold strictly above 60
sources.accessMethod: Opened current primary, council, church, museum and operator visitor pages, then scored the experience using the saved attraction method.
sources.limitations: Private façades and brief details remain heritage pins or trail stops rather than inflated attraction cards; current opening and pet policies can change.

sources.name: Crail visitor facilities and operator research
sources.organisation: Fife Council, Crail Museum and individual operators
sources.coverage: Food, trails, public parking, public toilets and art for Crail
sources.accessMethod: Opened official, responsible-body and operator visitor pages; linked exact current-place geometries
sources.limitations: Only Nethergate has a complete current council price-and-capacity page. Unknown Marketgate, harbour and Westgate payment details remain explicitly unpublished rather than inferred.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap current community places
sources.coverage: Food and drink, picnic/rest, art, memorial, historic, leisure, visitor, amenity, parking and natural-sight places within the Crail study area plus its 300m buffer.
sources.accessMethod: Read-only Overpass API query, then exact point-in-study-area filtering and source-ID/name-proximity deduplication.
sources.licence: Open Database Licence (ODbL) v1.0; © OpenStreetMap contributors.
sources.limitations: Current voluntary mapping only. Tags, names and locations may change; this optional icon layer is excluded from historic evidence, dates, heat scoring, totals and historic exports.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland Conservation Areas spatial data
sources.limitations: A conservation area is a historic-core study boundary, not an administrative settlement boundary.

sources.name: Welcome to Fife and Fife Council visitor evidence
sources.coverage: Crail visitor offer and responsible trail information
sources.accessMethod: Editorial review of official destination pages
sources.limitations: Opening, access and seasonal conditions must be checked with operators.

sources.name: Crail parking, food, dog-access and Treasure Trail re-audit
sources.organisation: Fife Council, Crail visitor bodies and individual operators
sources.coverage: Public visitor parking, current eating choices, place-specific dog access and the paid Crail Treasure Trail
sources.accessMethod: Current web research against named operator and visitor sources
sources.limitations: Marketgate North restrictions and Westgate details require on-site confirmation. Dog policies based on recent visitor evidence are labelled where the operator publishes no formal policy.

sources.name: Crail Parkopedia parking scrape and attraction dog-access audit
sources.organisation: Parkopedia, attraction operators and independent visitor sources
sources.coverage: Every Parkopedia car park returned for Crail and multiple-source dog-access checks for all four published attractions
sources.accessMethod: Live Parkopedia browser scrape plus targeted current web research
sources.limitations: Parkopedia lists 16 Nethergate spaces while Fife Council lists 15; the official count is retained. Museum and pottery pet access remain incompletely documented by their operators.
